record.original_question: For coverings and partitions by threshold graphs rather than cliques: first, if a graph family has the property that its nth member can be edge-covered by 2n threshold graphs but requires 3n threshold graphs for an edge-partition, is that gap best possible? Second, among graphs with 2n vertices and n² + 1 edges, what is the correct constant c such that one must contain a threshold subgraph with cn edges?

evidence.quote: I have a family of graphs such that the nth graph can be edge-covered by 2n threshold graphs, but requires 3n threshold graphs to edge-partition it. Is this best possible? ... What is the correct multiple of n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A threshold graph is a graph that can be constructed from a single vertex by repeatedly adding either an isolated vertex or a dominating vertex (a vertex adjacent to all previously added vertices). Given a graph $G$, an edge-cover of $G$ by threshold graphs is a collection of threshold subgraphs of $G$ whose edge sets together contain every edge of $G$; an edge-partition is such a collection in which the edge sets are pairwise disjoint and partition $E(G)$.

(a) Construct, or determine the best possible gap for, a sequence of graphs $\{G_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ with the following property: $G_n$ admits an edge-cover by $2n$ threshold graphs, but every edge-partition of $G_n$ into threshold graphs uses at least $3n$ parts. Is the ratio $3/2$ between the partition number and the cover number achievable, and is it best possible (i.e., can the gap between threshold-cover number and threshold-partition number on a single graph be larger than a factor of $3/2$, and if so, what is the supremum of this ratio)?

(b) Determine the largest constant $c > 0$ such that every graph on $2n$ vertices with at least $n^2 + 1$ edges contains a threshold subgraph with at least $cn$ edges. Equivalently, find
$$ c^* \;=\; \liminf_{n	o\infty} \; rac{1}{n}\;\min igl\{\, t(G) : |V(G)|=2n,\; |E(G)| \ge n^2+1 \, igr\}, $$
where $t(G)$ is the maximum number of edges of a threshold subgraph of $G$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for the specific gap between threshold edge-cover and threshold edge-partition numbers, and for the extremal constant $c$ in the second question, did not turn up a resolution. General references on threshold graphs and threshold dimension exist (e.g., recent work on bounds for threshold dimension), but no source verifying the optimal $2n$ vs $3n$ gap or the precise constant $c$ was found. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Some Bounds on the Threshold Dimension of Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work studies bounds for threshold dimension (minimum number of threshold graphs needed to edge-cover a graph), but does not resolve the cover-vs-partition gap question.
status_evidence.claim: The threshold dimension and threshold partition number are studied but no resolution of the specific 2n/3n gap is given.

status_evidence.title: An overview of graph covering and partitioning
status_evidence.snippet: General survey of graph covering and partitioning that does not address the specific extremal constants requested here.
status_evidence.claim: The specific extremal constants in the threshold-cover/partition problem are not resolved in this overview.
